findings.summary: The drift guard only sees whole-string ast.Constant literals that match KERNEL-[A-Z][A-Z0-9-]*. An id built by an f-string (f"KERNEL-{x}") or by concatenation (KERNEL_RULE_PREFIX + "X") gets past it without any failure. A scratch probe of the same scan logic confirmed this; it found only the implicitly concatenated literal. No product code builds an id that way today: a grep of src/e_agent finds 27 literal ids, exactly KERNEL_FINDING_IDS, and no f-string or prefix concatenation. A missed id also fails safe, because rule_stored stores it as a digest and nothing leaks. So this costs only readability in explain, not correctness. Optional hardening: have the test also fail on any JoinedStr or BinOp that starts with "KERNEL-" or KERNEL_RULE_PREFIX.

A KERNEL-* id that resolves only by its prefix still counts as resolved: RationaleCounts.rules.resolved counts it and it raises no repair, as R1-1 required. At rest, though, it goes under unresolved_rule_digests. RationaleRef's docstrings now overstate this: rules_considered says 'The rule ids that resolved' and unresolved_rule_digests says 'each rule id that resolved nothing'. Stored counts can therefore exceed len(rules_considered); the pure test has resolved == 3 with 2 ids listed. A docstring note would settle it: 'resolved and stored verbatim' / 'unresolved, or a KERNEL-* id the kernel does not emit'. This needs no behaviour change.
